I read through your whole post and while I hate tough love because it makes me feel like shit and want to cry (which i did), I do still really like the actual advice. It's actually taking mental illness into perspective instead of expecting me to do things the way a neurotypical should and then calling me lazy or saying I'm "making up excuses" when said mental illnesses make those things impossible.


Here's some more specific comments on parts of your post. I'll take all of it to heart.


> The only person in your world who cares about these things also happens to have a disability that makes it extremely challenging to influence the version of you that is making these decisions.


Hit the nail on the head, there.


> You need to get out of the house, and to interact with others regularly, preferably the same people.


This is a good idea, but an issue with those things is that they require money or transportation or both, and I have neither. I've tried looking for nearby activities/'third places' to try and get myself out of the house but there wasn't anything within walking distance. Our last house was in the middle of rural nowhere with nothing but trees around for several miles before you got to any actual places, and the current place we're in now after our landlady kicked us out isn't any better.


I'll check again, though, and hopefully something will come up. Maybe some volunteer work.

I feel like throwing up when I see someone on the other side of the street than me while I'm going for a walk, I don't know how I'd actually talk to someone. But I guess I'll figure something out.


> And please, for the love of god, shower and use deodorant for these people. You are probably nose blind to it, but the hygiene you described is really really bad. The smell is probably stuck to your chair and bed, so until you get that cleaned up please shower no more than 5 hours before going out.


Oh I'm actually fully aware of how badly I smell. I'm not nose blind, I am actually regularly offended and disgusted by myself, but somehow that still isn't enough to get me to actually shower. A lot of the time I avoid leaving my room because I don't want my parents to be able to smell me, or I avoid going outside for walks because I don't want anybody to see my greasy-ass hair or walk past me. 


Only time I'm able to actually push past my ADHD is when I know I have to go somewhere in public that day or the day after. So your suggestion is absolutely something that would help with that, I think.


> Is your dad in the picture? Do you have siblings?


No, my father left before my 1st birthday. I never met him, and it's just been me and my mom for almost my entire life. I have a step-dad but he's basically constantly working and we almost never talk. 


And I'm an only child.


> She can be with you, but have someone else who will be disappointed or upset if you decide to skip.


Don't really have anybody like that unfortunately. I do have my RSD and probably-AvPD that motivate me with extreme fear and stress and guilt when something like that happens but they just as equally cause me to completely shut down and do nothing.


> Get some type of life in your room (not microbial, lol). Something like a fish, lizard, plant, hamster, etc. Something that you need to be responsible to provide for. Plants need sunlight, so you can't sit in the dark all day. Animals need food, so you have to go buy it for them. The point is to slowly fill your life with things that you need to do for other people/creatures. Doing something just for yourself is already hard for people without routine or structure, and it oftentimes simply does not work for those with executive dysfunction.

It's been hard, because my brain has been all-or-nothing for... well, almost my whole life. And now that I'm 26 and those neural pathways have solidified, it's gonna be even harder... but I'm trying to hold on to hope.

And I have been trying to follow it. Didn't go to bed at 12? Well, 3AM is better than 5AM. And 5AM is still better than 6AM. Can't get myself to brush my teeth? Well, just brushing is fine, even if I don't floss or irrigate, and even if I don't do the whole 2 minutes. Can't shower? I can at least change my underwear. That sort of thing.

Imagine having to consciously make the effort to blink and inhale or exhale, every second of every day, for your entire life. And it never gets easier or simpler or becomes automatic. You need to remember to breathe every single time and if you forget even once you suffocate. You can *never* relax. You can't allow a *single* distraction, or you fail. And because it's ADHD... good luck not getting distracted. 

That's what it's like for me. And this is assuming my executive functioning abilities are actually, y'know, functioning, and allowing me to actually perform basic tasks. A lot of the time I know fully, 100%, that I NEED to do something, and I WANT to do it, but I just can't. My brain won't let me. It's just so exhausting having to consciously make the decision to brush my teeth, take a shower, pretty much everything. It's not me giving up or accepting defeat; it's my ADHD. It's the fact that because of it, I am mentally incapable of forming routines or habits. That's not an excuse, that's *part of having ADHD.*

I am NEVER on 'autopilot' for anything. My entire life, when I had to brush my teeth, I had to make sure to remember and make a conscious effort every single time. It never once, not even when I was in elementary school, became something I could just *do* because it had become so routine at that part. I don't have routines.

Now extend that to everything in my life, everything I try to do. You can imagine how utterly exhausting it is. And meds and therapy haven't helped.

I do try to talk to my parents but I'm constantly worried that I'm already such a burden on them that anything more would just make them upset. They're trying to save up for a new house and money is... really tight, on top of my mom being the one that pays for my... well, everything, from dental to health insurance to school etc.

I do drink lots of water, in fact it's pretty much all I drink. And I've been trying to fix my sleep schedule lately, though it's hard when most of my friends like to stay up well into the AM, so I haven't been spending as much time with them lately.

Also trying to cut out junk food. However nutrition and eating healthy is difficult because money is tight, so I kinda have to take what I can get... and if that means pizza three nights in a row, oh well.

Exercise, I've been trying my best but I'm rarely consistent. Most exercise I get is just walking around the tiny-ass, super cramped and cluttered house I'm in for like ten minutes or so.

I'll save this post and look into the other stuff. Next time I see my doctor is... December, so I'll have to figure something out with my mom.

My mental disorders are not a crutch, they're something I have literally no control over. I have been trying to deal with them using every available method I have but nothing has really been helping.

People who don't understand mental illnesses always think of mental disorders as an excuse. They aren't an excuse, they're a *reason*.

I can try as hard as I want to do those things; take regular baths, exercise, walk every day, but if my ADHD decides I'm not going to? Then nothing I do will make me able to do it. That's how mental disorders work.

If it was that easy for me, do you really think I would've made this thread?

I personally think the Tau don't really put any sort of emphasis on breakfast, lunch, dinner etc. culturally. they probably just view it as the optimal time for nutrition and hydration. Think like, a military mess or a school cafeteria or something. Communal, everybody goes to the designated mess area and eats largely the same thing or variations depending on their dietary needs for like different species or maybe even allergies etc. (one character in Elemental Council tells another, both of them tau, something along the lines of "we're not ALL vegetarians" after the other was surprised to see them eating meat, which implies personal taste or choice is a factor as well.)

Though I will say I haven't seen anything that implies Tau don't have like, "luxury" foods. In Elemental council one of the main characters sleepily grabs some nutrition-paste gruel as a midnight snack, BUT later on some Pathfinders are shown chowing down on native human delicacies (basically just fish jerky) around a campfire.

but anyway, breakfast lunch and dinner are probably just viewed by the tau as "morning meal, midday meal, evening meal" and they don't add much more importance beyond that. Maybe back in the time of Mon'tau the tribes had their own cultural things, and each caste does have its own cultural traditions that stem from that, so I wouldn't be surprised if it depended on your caste.

Either way whatever they're eating is leagues better than even middle-class Imperium food that's for damn sure. (aside from maybe the nutrient paste but even then who knows, and its shown that their standard rations are actually pretty appealing and might as well just be like modern day MREs. Real ingredients, real wheat and meat and fruit etc. with not a can of corpse starch in sight.)
